**Solution 1 (answer 1): REJECT.** The straight midpoint cut is valid, but non-straight staircases also work. For example, cut the 2024×2025 rectangle along the lattice path from the top side at x=506 down to the bottom side at x=1518, with horizontal jumps of 506 at heights y=675 and y=1350. Translating the right piece by (−506, +675) tiles a 1518×2700 rectangle exactly, and 1518×2700 = 4,098,600. So the count is at least 2.

**Solution 2 (answer 21): REJECT.** Its claim that every smaller side in [1012, 2023] is achievable is unjustified. The pieces' bounding boxes constrain the possible dimensions far more tightly. Working through the constraints gives a much smaller set of achievable rectangles.

**Solution 3 (answer 7): REJECT.** Several of its rectangles are impossible. A top-to-bottom cut has both pieces spanning the full height 2025, so each piece's horizontal extent must fit within the short side a. Their horizontal extents sum to at least 2024, which forces a ≥ 1012. This rules out 506×8100, 44×93150, 675×6072, 405×10120, 225×18216 and 45×91080. Its Type A/B parametrization also misses valid cuts such as 1518×2700.

Working the constraints out fully (top-to-bottom cuts with n | 2025 and (n+1) | 2024, plus left-to-right cuts with n | 2024 and (n+1) | 2025), I get six achievable rectangles: 1012×4050, 1518×2700, 1980×2070, 1350×3036, 1620×2530, and 1800×2277. This is my own derivation, which I have not checked against an independent source, but none of the three proposed answers (1, 21, 7) matches it.

VERDICT 1: REJECT
VERDICT 2: REJECT
VERDICT 3: REJECT
